title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: A refractory high-entropy alloy (likely a NbMoTaW or similar system) in a disordered solid solution state
recollection.intervention: Thermal annealing or specific processing to induce chemical short-range order (CSRO) without forming long-range order or secondary phases
recollection.structure: A single-phase body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solution exhibiting local chemical ordering (CSRO) rather than a completely random atomic distribution
recollection.mechanism: The CSRO reduces the phonon scattering caused by mass and strain fluctuations inherent in random solid solutions, thereby increasing the phonon mean free path and thermal conductivity, contrary to the typical expectation that disorder suppresses thermal conductivity in HEAs
recollection.results: A significant increase in lattice thermal conductivity (likely by a factor of 2 or more compared to the disordered state) at elevated temperatures, potentially reaching values comparable to or exceeding those of pure refractory metals, while maintaining high strength
recollection.note: This is a best guess based on the title's explicit claim and recent trends in high-entropy alloy research (2023-2024) regarding the role of short-range order on thermal transport. The specific alloy system and exact quantitative values are not in my training data as this paper appears to be very recent or hypothetical in the context of my knowledge cutoff.

score.note: The recollection generically identifies inducing CSRO but incorrectly attributes it to annealing rather than Monte Carlo-controlled ordering. It correctly notes a BCC alloy with local ordering, but misses the specific B2-like HfTi/TiZr clusters and percolative pathways. The reduced strain/lattice-distortion scattering mechanism is correctly recalled, though the percolation and phonon-DOS effects are omitted. The claimed factor-of-two increase is far from the actual ~12% increase.
